problem: The pricing controls were visible in production but could stop reacting after runtime DOM replacement, while English routing still depended on client-side translation fallback and could remain Dutch or show a switching error.
root_cause: The rescue controller initialized only on one DOM lifecycle path and did not re-synchronize after later DOM replacement. Separately, production had STATIC_I18N_NETWORK=0, so /en routes could be emitted as untranslated fallback documents and depended on a runtime translation request instead of carrying English content at release time.
prevention: Pricing interaction uses delegated capture-phase click, touchend and keyboard handling and initializes both before and after DOMContentLoaded as appropriate.
A MutationObserver re-synchronizes lifecycle, package and billing state after runtime child-list replacement.
The pricing interaction asset URL is versioned whenever the rescue controller changes so returning mobile clients do not retain stale JavaScript.
Production localized builds enable static translation; deploy previews remain deterministic and offline.
Regression tests assert the self-repair controller and the production-versus-preview i18n environment contract.
Do not mark the incident LIVE_BEWEZEN until the exact merged candidate is deployed and both /prijzen and /en/prijzen are read back from production.
